answer: Hypothesis: In the PCA of forms of capital analysed in 100-year time slices, the PC1 value at the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is markedly higher — approximately +1.66 in standardised score units (PC1 explaining 76% of variance) — whereas the six subsequent slices from 1000 to 500 BCE cluster much lower, between about −0.74 and +0.34 (mean ≈ −0.28), meaning the 1100 BCE level sits roughly 1.9 units (about 4 standard deviations) above the rest of the period, driven by high Z-values for depot hoards (ZHort), copper/gold (ZCU_AU), house size (Zhausgr) and monument count (ZMonument) at 1100 BCE, after which all these capital indicators collapse and PC1 drifts down to its lowest values around 600–500 BCE.

payload.hypothesis: In the PCA of forms of capital analysed in 100-year time slices, the PC1 value at the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is markedly higher (approximately +1.66, with PC1 explaining ~76% of variance) than the six subsequent slices from 1000 to 500 BCE, which cluster between about −0.74 and +0.34 (mean ≈ −0.28); the 1100 BCE level sits roughly 1.9 standardised units (~4 SD) above the rest of the period, driven by high Z-values for depot hoards, copper/gold, house size and monument count at 1100 BCE, after which these capital indicators collapse and PC1 declines to its lowest values around 600–500 BCE.
payload.workflow: Loaded capital.csv (decimal-comma format), dropped group/color, used all 12 pre-Z-scored capital variables as-is. Rows already sit at 100-year slices; the 7 rows 1100–500 BCE form the YBA window. Fitted PCA (SVD) on the pooled 7-slice YBA window, extracted per-slice PC1 scores, and compared the 1100 BCE score against the 1000–500 BCE band. Robustness: (1) PCA refit on the full 39-row record — 1100 BCE remains the positive outlier; (2) refit with zero-variance columns ZSichel/ZKeform dropped — scores identical.
